public_rationale: OpenAI's contemporary evaluation acknowledges continuing factual errors in GPT-5.4 and compares them with GPT-5.2. That supports the ordinary claim that LLMs remain prone to hallucination. The same evidence documents improvement, so it does not support an additional claim that the problem is immutable or that every answer is unreliable.
limitations: This is a provider's own evaluation.
The prompts were selected from reported factual errors and do not estimate error frequency across all usage.
The conclusion concerns recurring factual failures, not universal uselessness.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are inherently unreliable and prone to hallucination.

statement.excerpt: There’s also the underlying unreliability of hallucination-prone Large Language Models.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that contemporary general-purpose LLMs retain a recurring tendency to produce false factual content.
The exact quotation does not say that every answer is unreliable or that hallucinations can never be reduced.
For this ongoing technical observation, I use current-year model evaluations available through the post: January 1–April 28, 2026.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations of contemporary LLMs demonstrate recurring factual errors or fabricated content.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show that contemporary general-purpose LLMs reliably avoid factual fabrication across the ordinary tasks covered by the claim.

evidence.explanation: At release, OpenAI reported that GPT-5.4 produced 33% fewer false individual claims and 18% fewer responses containing errors than GPT-5.2 on prompts selected from user-reported factual errors. These reductions establish remaining factual failures while also documenting improvement.
